import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_2/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_2/training_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_2/training_2.csv"

df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)  # Source3_2_0: ['user_id', 'movie_id', 'rating', 'timestamp']
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)  # Source3_2_1: ['movie_id', 'title', 'genres']
df2 = pd.read_csv(source2_path, index_col=0)  # Source3_2_2: ['user_id', 'gender', 'age', 'occupation', 'zip']

# Operation History:
# 1) JOIN Source3_2_0 and Source3_2_1 on movie_id
df01 = pd.merge(df0, df1[['movie_id', 'title']], on='movie_id', how='inner')

# 2) JOIN the above result with Source3_2_2 on user_id
df_final = pd.merge(df01, df2[['user_id', 'age', 'occupation']], on='user_id', how='inner')

# According to target schema:
# ['title': string, 'user_id': float, 'age': float, 'occupation': float, 'movie_id': integer, 'rating': float, 'timestamp': float]

# Ensure correct dtypes and column order
df_final = df_final[['title', 'user_id', 'age', 'occupation', 'movie_id', 'rating', 'timestamp']]

# Convert types to match target schema
df_final['title'] = df_final['title'].astype(str)
df_final['user_id'] = df_final['user_id'].astype(float)
df_final['age'] = df_final['age'].astype(float)
df_final['occupation'] = df_final['occupation'].astype(float)
df_final['movie_id'] = df_final['movie_id'].astype(int)
df_final['rating'] = df_final['rating'].astype(float)
df_final['timestamp'] = df_final['timestamp'].astype(float)

# Write the result to the target path
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_2/target_multisource.csv"
df_final.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_2/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_2/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_2/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source3_2_0 and Source3_2_1 on movie_id
join_0_1 = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Join the above result with Source3_2_2 on user_id
joined = pd.merge(join_0_1, source2, on="user_id", how="inner")

# Group by the leftmost non-float columns in target schema that are unique identifiers:
# According to target schema and hints, group by: title (string), user_id (float but used as id), age (float), occupation (float), movie_id (int)
# Aggregate rating and timestamp by mean to match target averages and reduce duplicates
grouped = joined.groupby(
    ["title", "user_id", "age", "occupation", "movie_id"], as_index=False
).agg({
    "rating": "mean",
    "timestamp": "mean"
})

# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
final_df = grouped[["title", "user_id", "age", "occupation", "movie_id", "rating", "timestamp"]]

# Write output
final_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_2/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
